prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck—best depends on the specifics of your case (severity of injuries, fault issues, insurance limits, whether you’ll need a trial, etc.). Instead of one name, here’s a quick, practical way to find the right attorney in Houston and what to look for.

How to choose the right lawyer
- Look for relevant experience: lots of car-crash cases and recent experience with cases similar to yours (serious injury, catastrophic injury, wrongful death, uninsured motorist, etc.).
- Trial experience and resources: a firm that will actually try the case if needed usually gets better settlement offers.
- Board certification: in Texas, TBLS Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law is a strong credential (not required, but meaningful).
- Track record: recent verdicts/settlements, client testimonials, and peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell AV, Super Lawyers).
- Communication and accessibility: clear point of contact, timely updates.
- Fee structure: most take cases on contingency (commonly ~33% if settled before suit; may be higher if suit/filed). Confirm how expenses are handled.
- Local reputation: local judges, insurance adjusters, and opposing counsel know the firm’s reputation—this matters.

Where to look
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (TBLS) list of board-certified personal injury trial lawyers.
- Houston Bar Association lawyer referral service.
- Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, and local legal directories and Google/Yelp reviews.
- Recommendations from friends/family or other attorneys you trust.

Questions to ask at a free consult
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled in the last 3 years?
- How many of those went to trial and what were the results?
- Who in the firm will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your fee and how are expenses handled if we don’t win?
- What do you think my case is worth and why?
- What is the expected timeline and next steps?
- Can you provide references from past clients?

What to bring to the initial meeting
- Police report, photos of the crash scene/vehicles/injuries
- Medical records and bills, prescription list
- Insurance information (your policy and the other driver’s if available)
- Contact info for witnesses
- Any correspondence from insurance companies

Important deadlines
- Texas generally has a 2-year statute of limitations for most personal injury claims, so contact an attorney promptly. (If a government entity is involved, different, much shorter notice deadlines can apply.)
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers or accept the first settlement offer before talking to a lawyer.

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific outcome or dollar amount
- Refusal to put the fee agreement in writing
- Poor communication or multiple unanswered calls
- Lowball flat-fee offers without a clear plan

If you’d like, I can:
- Help narrow options by neighborhood/zip code in Houston and list several highly rated firms (I’ll need your zip code or area), or
- Give a template of questions to email/ask multiple attorneys to compare them.

Tell me your location and a brief summary of the crash (injuries, fault/insurance situation) and I’ll help you find and evaluate attorneys in Houston.
